title: Unauthenticated pickle deserialization in the basket cookie
description: The basket cookie is entirely controlled by the client, but is passed to pickle.loads without authentication or integrity protection. A remote attacker can supply a crafted cookie that executes arbitrary Python code when any basket endpoint calls read_basket().
evidence: read_basket() base64-decodes request.cookies['basket'] and calls pickle.loads(raw) at line 20; with_basket() writes an unsigned pickle back to the client at lines 26-28.

title: Passwordless JWT refresh accepts attacker-forged claims
description: The refresh endpoint decodes the submitted JWT with signature verification disabled, trusts its sub claim to select a database user, and then signs a fresh token. Anyone can submit a hand-crafted token with the subject of another user, including a staff user, and obtain a valid bearer token for that account.
evidence: jwt.decode(token, options={'verify_signature': False}) is used at line 101, followed by load_user(claims.get('sub')) and make_token(user) at lines 104-107.

title: JWT signing key is hard-coded in source
description: The application uses a fixed, source-visible SECRET_KEY for HS256 bearer tokens. Anyone who obtains the repository or source artifact can forge tokens for arbitrary user IDs and roles, compromising every authenticated endpoint.
evidence: SECRET_KEY is assigned the literal value 'hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d' at line 3 and is used for JWT signing and verification in shopapi/auth.py lines 27 and 42.

title: Authentication failures are swallowed by require_auth
description: require_auth catches its own abort(401) exception and still invokes the protected view with g.user set to None. Endpoints whose view does not dereference g.user can therefore be called without authentication; notably, order lookup exposes any order and gift-card balance exposes card balances.
evidence: The abort(401) at lines 53-54 is caught by the broad Exception handler at line 55, which then calls f(*args, **kwargs) at line 58. shopapi/orders.py:49 calls get_order() without an ownership check, and shopapi/giftcards.py:16 returns a balance after the bypassed decorator.

title: Trailing-slash admin refund route bypasses staff authorization
description: The global admin guard compares the raw request path against the registered rule strings. The refund rule accepts both slash forms, but only the no-slash form is in admin_paths, so POST /admin/refunds/ skips the staff check and can issue refunds anonymously.
evidence: staff_only_admin() gates only when request.path is in admin_paths at lines 36-41. The route is registered with strict_slashes=False in shopapi/admin.py:52; a test request to /admin/refunds/ returned 200 and created a refund without Authorization.

title: Product search concatenates attacker input into SQL
description: The q query parameter is interpolated directly into a SQL string. An unauthenticated attacker can inject SQL syntax to alter the query and extract data from the SQLite database.
evidence: The query at lines 40-42 builds the LIKE expression using q by string concatenation and executes it without parameters.

title: Staff review report is vulnerable to SQL injection
description: A customer's display name is inserted into a SQL statement using an f-string. A customer can set display_name to SQL syntax, and any staff member viewing the report then causes the injected query to execute.
evidence: The report query contains f"WHERE r.author_name = '{customer['display_name']}' ORDER BY r.id DESC" at line 80; display_name is user-controlled via shopapi/auth.py:124.

title: Review bodies are rendered as trusted HTML
description: Authenticated users can submit arbitrary review text, but the product template marks each review body safe. A malicious reviewer can store HTML or script content that executes for every visitor to the product page.
evidence: products.py:90 stores the submitted body without sanitization, and product.html line 13 renders r.body with the Jinja safe filter.

title: Payment timeout fails open as a successful payment
description: If the payment provider times out, the exception handler sets status to paid and marks the order processing with the full total. An attacker or network condition that causes provider requests to time out can obtain fulfillment without a confirmed payment.
evidence: The requests.Timeout handler at lines 39-42 assigns status = 'paid'; lines 43-46 then set paid_pence = total_pence and transition the order to processing.

title: Payment webhook trusts an unvalidated amount
description: After checking only the order ID signature, the webhook writes the event-supplied amount into paid_pence without requiring it to equal the order total or checking that it is positive. A signed paid event can therefore mark an underpaid order as paid or create inconsistent payment state.
evidence: The paid branch assigns int(event.get('amount_pence', 0)) directly to paid_pence at lines 70-71; the signature is computed only over order_id at lines 53-55.

title: Passwords are stored as unsalted SHA-256 digests
description: SHA-256 is a fast general-purpose hash and is used without a salt or work factor. A database disclosure enables efficient offline cracking of user passwords, including the staff account if it uses a reused or guessable password.
evidence: hash_password() returns hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest() at lines 15-16, and the resulting digest is stored directly in users.password_hash at auth.py:77.
